simple.meaning: יְקָר (yᵉqâr) is a Hebrew word meaning “glory, honour.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: יְקָר (H3367) appears 7 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Daniel 2:6, with occurrences in Daniel.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to יְקָר (H3367) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in יְקָר (H3367) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: יְקָר (yᵉqâr) / H3367 is traced through Daniel 2:6, Daniel 2:37, Daniel 4:27, Daniel 4:33 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

firstOccurrence.englishText: But if you show the dream and its interpretation, you will receive of me gifts and rewards and great honor. Therefore show me the dream and its interpretation.”

timeline.evidenceText: But if you show the dream and its interpretation, you will receive of me gifts and rewards and great honor. Therefore show me the dream and its interpretation.”
You, O king, are king of kings, to whom the God of heaven has given the kingdom, the power, the strength, and the glory.

Therefore, O king, let my counsel be acceptable to you, and break off your sins by righteousness, and your iniquities by showing mercy to the poor. Perhaps there may be a lengthening of your tranquility.”

This was fulfilled the same hour on Nebuchadnezzar. He was driven from men, and ate grass as oxen, and his body was wet with the dew of the sky, until his hair had grown like eagles’ feathers, and his nails like birds’ claws.
“You, king, the Most High God gave Nebuchadnezzar your father the kingdom, and greatness, and glory, and majesty.
But when his heart was lifted up, and his spirit was hardened so that he dealt proudly, he was deposed from his kingly throne, and they took his glory from him.

Dominion was given him, and glory, and a kingdom, that all the peoples, nations, and languages should serve him. His dominion is an everlasting dominion, which will not pass away, and his kingdom that which will not be destroyed.
